{children}
15 } 16 ``` 17 18 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher 19 export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) { 20 return
{children}
21 } 22 ``` 23 24 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`. 25 26 A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `` and `` tags and other globally shared UI. 27 28 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 29 export default function RootLayout({ 30 children, 31 }: { 32 children: React.ReactNode 33 }) { 34 return ( 35 36 {children} 37 38 ) 39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 43 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 44 return ( 45 46 {children} 47 48 ) 49 } 50 ``` 51 52 ## Reference 53 54 ### Props 55 56 #### `children` (required) 57 58 Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable. 59 60 #### `params` (optional) 61 62 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout. 63 64 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher 65 export default async function Layout({ 66 children, 67 params, 68 }: { 69 children: React.ReactNode 70 params: Promise<{ team: string }> 71 }) { 72 const { team } = await params 73 } 74 ``` 75 76 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher 77 export default async function Layout({ children, params }) { 78 const { team } = await params 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 | Example Route | URL | `params` | 83 | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | 84 | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js` | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>` | 85 | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` | 86 | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js` | `/blog/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 87 88 - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 89 - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 90 91 ### Layout Props Helper 92 93 You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper. 94 95 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 96 export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) { 97 return ( 98
99 {props.children} 100 {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */} 101 {/* {props.analytics} */} 102
103 ) 104 } 105 ``` 106 107 > **Good to know**: 108 > 109 > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`. 110 > - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported. 111 112 ### Root Layout 113 114 The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`. 115 116 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 117 export default function RootLayout({ 118 children, 119 }: { 120 children: React.ReactNode 121 }) { 122 return ( 123 124 {children} 125 126 ) 127 } 128 ``` 129 130 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 131 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 132 return ( 133 134 {children} 135 136 ) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 - The root layout **must** define `` and `` tags. 141 - You should **not** manually add `` tags such as `` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements. 142 - You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches: 143 - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js` 144 - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories. 145 - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation). 146 - The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. 147 148 ## Caveats 149 150 ### Request Object 151 152 Layouts are cached in the client during navigation to avoid unnecessary server requests. 153 154 [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) do not rerender. 3	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4	---
5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18	
19	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20	    slug: post.slug,
21	  }))
22	}
23	
24	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26	export default async function Page({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { slug } = await params
32	  // ...
33	}
34	```
35	
36	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher

47	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49	  const { slug } = await params
50	  // ...
51	}
52	```
53	
54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-build-time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62	
63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70	
71	## Returns
72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74	
75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77	
78	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83	
84	## Single Dynamic Segment
85

94	// - /product/2

103	}

206	## Examples
207	
208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
213	
214	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
215	export async function generateStaticParams() {
216	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
217	
218	  return posts.map((post) => ({
219	    slug: post.slug,
220	  }))
221	}
222	```
223	
224	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
225	export async function generateStaticParams() {
226	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
227	
228	  return posts.map((post) => ({
229	    slug: post.slug,
230	  }))
231	}
232	```
233	
234	#### Subset of paths at build time
235	
236	To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
237	
238	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
239	export async function generateStaticParams() {
240	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
241	
242	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
243	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
244	    slug: post.slug,
245	  }))
246	}
247	```
248	
249	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
250	export async function generateStaticParams() {
251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252	
253	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```
259	
260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```
275	
276	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
277	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
278	export const dynamicParams = false
279	
280	export async function generateStaticParams() {
281	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
282	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
283	
284	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
285	    slug: post.slug,
286	  }))
287	}
288	```
289	
290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```
334	
335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
336	export async function generateStaticParams() {
337	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
338	}
339	
340	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
341	  const { id } = await params
342	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
343	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
344	}
345	```
346	
347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
352	export async function generateStaticParams() {
353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}
355	
356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```
371	
372	See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
373	
374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
390	
391	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
392	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
393	export async function generateStaticParams() {
394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```
410	
411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
412	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
432	// Generate segments for [category]
433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))
458	}
459	
460	export default function Layout({ params }) {
461	  // ...
462	}
463	```
464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
470	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
516	
517	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
518	export async function generateStaticParams({
519	  params: { category },
520	}: {
521	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
522	}) {
523	  const products = await fetch(
524	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
525	  ).then((res) => res.json())
526	
527	  return products.map((product) => ({
528	    product: product.id,
529	  }))
530	}
531	```
532	
533	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
534	
535	## Version History
536	
537	| Version   | Changes                            |
538	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
539	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:

290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"

296	  return []
297	}
298	```

300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs.

316	### With Route Handlers

323	}

328	) {

374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.

394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```

411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher

413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher

433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))

464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher

471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>

492	}

497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function

514

42	## `generateMetadata` function
43	
44	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45	
46	Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47	
48	Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52	
53	type Props = {
54	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56	}
57	
58	export async function generateMetadata(
59	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
60	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
61	): Promise<Metadata> {
62	  // read route params
63	  const { id } = await params
64	
65	  // fetch data
66	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67	
68	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70	
71	  return {
72	    title: product.title,
73	    openGraph: {
74	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80	```

4	---
5	
6	The `notFound` function allows you to render the [`not-found file`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found) within a route segment as well as inject a [`<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) tag for search engines.
7	
8	## `notFound()`
9	
10	Invoking the `notFound()` function throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment in which it was thrown. Specifying a [**not-found** file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found) allows you to gracefully handle such errors by rendering a Not Found UI within the segment.
11	
12	```jsx filename="app/user/[id]/page.js"
13	import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
14	
15	async function fetchUser(id) {
16	  const res = await fetch('https://...')
17	  if (!res.ok) return undefined
18	  return res.json()
19	}
20	
21	export default async function Profile({ params }) {
22	  const { id } = await params
23	  const user = await fetchUser(id)
24	
25	  if (!user) {
26	    notFound()
27	  }
28	
29	  // ...
30	}
31	```
32	
33	> **Good to know**: `notFound()` does not require you to use `return notFound()` due to using the TypeScript [`never`](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/functions.html#never) type.
34	
35	## Version History
36	
37	| Version   | Changes                |
38	| --------- | ---------------------- |
39	| `v13.0.0` | `notFound` introduced. |
40

6	The `dynamicParams` option allows you to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with [generateStaticParams](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params).
